Fixed by wiring the EXISTING fail-loud helper waitAssistantFacadeReady, already used by two other specs, into the four affected tests. A t.Skipf on 503 would also have turned the lane green and would have been precisely the wrong fix, reproducing the pattern BUG-069-005 exists to remove; the chosen helper calls t.Fatalf on deadline so a genuine wiring failure still surfaces red. Verified the delivered implement phase as a specialist rather than re-implementing it, and corrected the phase claim from parent-expanded to specialist because a dispatch that returned no output is not a missing capability. Read internal/assistant/httpadapter/dedup.go directly: the cache key is turnDedupKey{userDigest, transport, messageID} where begin() hashes the user ID with sha256.Sum256 and pins transport to TransportName, so auth scoping is structural and a same-ID turn from another identity cannot collide. The lease carries owner bool; the first caller for a key executes and every later caller gets a non-owner lease whose wait() selects on entry.ready against ctx.Done(), so a duplicate blocks on the owner instead of re-executing yet still unblocks if its own client drops. complete() is owner-guarded and re-checks entry identity under the lock before stamping expiresAt and closing ready. Retention is bounded on both axes: removeExpiredLocked drops completed entries past TTL and evictOldestCompletedLocked walks the LRU list from the back and evicts only entries already marked completed, so an in-flight turn is never evicted out from under its waiters and a cache saturated with in-flight work refuses new unique work rather than corrupting a live lease. Read the adapter.go wiring: line 75 builds the cache from HTTPTurnDedupCapacity=16384 plus ConversationTTL and the injected clock; line 383 calls begin() with a sha256 fingerprint of the marshalled request, which is what converts a changed payload under a reused ID into 409 transport_message_id_conflict at line 385 instead of a silent second execution, with capacity exhaustion as 503 at line 388; the non-owner branch at line 396 replays cached status and body under a fresh Trace.RequestID and returns without reaching facade.Handle, while the owner branch invokes facade.Handle exactly once and completes on both outcomes, 500 at line 409 and 200 at line 428, so an accepted failure is replayed rather than retried. Confirmation run of ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run TestHTTPTurnDedup --verbose returned exit 0 with 8 RUN, 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, each PASS paired with its own === RUN line. The httpadapter ok line reports a real 0.083s duration and does NOT carry the [no tests to run] suffix, which is the discriminator against a vacuous pass and is meaningful rather than incidental because the same run emits that suffix 203 times for packages the selector correctly matches nothing in. Q3 found no scaffolding, TODO, or orphan symbol in dedup.go, and one structural finding: evictCompletedLocked's guard len(entries) > capacity is unreachable because the single insertion site at line 100 sits behind the line 91 capacity guard and no other path grows the map. It was deliberately retained, not deleted, because begin makes room for one entry while this function trims to the bound unconditionally, and that is what makes HTTPTurnDedupCapacity a hard DoS memory ceiling rather than one contingent on a single guard staying correct. Verification with no code changed: ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run TestHTTPTurnDedup --verbose gave 8 RUN, 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0, and ./smackerel.sh check exited 0 with no config drift. The E2E suite was not run; it holds a flock suite lock and this phase produced no source edit for it to cover.

Bounded operational review of the process-local turn-dedup surface at HEAD 0c200519. Verdict PARTIALLY_STABLE: the concurrency design is sound and no source file was changed, with three findings recorded as Discovered Issues rows dated 2026-08-23 naming their owning artifact. Q1, the single-replica premise was confirmed by search rather than assumed; grep for replicas across docker-compose files, deploy, and config returns exactly one hit, deploy/README.md:51, which is prose about what a target params.yaml may contain, so no compose file or SST key sets a replica count. The blast radius if that changes is worth stating precisely because two guarantees fail in opposite directions: replay degrades to a second facade execution, which for a CaptureRoute turn double-persists the prompt at adapter.go:424, but the conflict guarantee inverts, since a changed payload under a reused ID is rejected 409 at adapter.go:385 today and on a replica holding no entry is instead executed and answered 200. The safety property flips from refuse to execute, which is why scale-out needs the durable design named in Open Findings rather than a larger local cache. Q2, all three retention mechanisms are present and were re-derived from source: capacity guard at dedup.go:91 surfacing 503 at adapter.go:388, TTL expiry driven from the head of begin so there is no timer goroutine to leak, and completed-only eviction at dedup.go:134 and dedup.go:153 so an in-flight turn is never evicted from under its waiters. What the bound does not cover is bytes. HTTPTurnDedupCapacity=16384 counts entries while each retains a whole TurnResponse whose Body has no cap in this adapter, and the only size limit on the path, http.MaxBytesReader at middleware.go:109, bounds the request not the retained response, so the ceiling is 16384 times the largest emitted body, roughly 64 MB at 4 KB and roughly 1 GB at 64 KB. Compounding it, adapter.go:75 reuses ConversationTTL, set to conversation_ttl_seconds 86400 at config/smackerel.yaml:1360, so a transport idempotency window that exists to absorb a seconds-to-minutes retry is held 24 hours; the defect is the coupling of two unrelated durations to one knob. Q3, I agree with retaining evictCompletedLocked and re-derived its unreachability independently rather than inheriting it. begin makes room for one entry while that function trims to the bound unconditionally, which is what keeps the ceiling from depending on line 91 staying correct, at a cost of one integer compare under a mutex already held. The caveat belonging with that agreement is that an unreachable guard cannot be covered by a test and can rot silently, which is exactly why the reachable guard must carry coverage, and it does: TestHTTPTurnDedup_CacheRejectsUniqueWorkWhenAllSlotsAreInFlight drives dedup.go:91 to its refusal branch and passed here. Q4, the readiness-budget split is real but its failure mode is benign in direction and the count given to this phase was low. The helper calls t.Fatalf on deadline at nl_facade_readiness_helper_test.go:54, so an under-budgeted site yields a loud false RED rather than a silent false GREEN. There are five 90s sites, not four: nl_facade_routing:27, annotation_classifier:41, nl_rate_disambig:34, nl_find_replacement:33, and legacy_retirement_notice:135 whose timeout argument sits on line 138 where a single-line grep does not show it, against four 5-minute sites added this session. All five predate this session and the helper header attributes it to Spec 076 SCOPE-4a, so harmonization is owned by specs/076-assistant-completion-rescope. Q5, surfaced rather than asked and the most operationally significant: a recovered panic orphans an in-flight entry permanently. lease.complete runs on exactly two paths, adapter.go:409 and adapter.go:428, and neither call site is protected by a defer, the handler's only defer being the body close at adapter.go:347, while middleware.Recoverer sits at internal/api/router.go:44 above the route registered at router.go:98. The process survives the panic and the entry stays completed false, which both reclamation paths skip by design, so the transport message ID is poisoned permanently, a retry blocking as a non-owner waiter until its own context expires instead of re-executing, and one of 16384 slots is consumed for the process lifetime. Severity medium and latent: no facade panic was observed here, and what lifts it above theory is that Recoverer exists at all, meaning the repo treats panics as survivable and this cache is the component on that path that does not. Verification with no code changed: ./smackerel.sh check exited 0 with config in sync and no env_file drift, and ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run TestHTTPTurnDedup --verbose gave 8 RUN, 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0, with the httpadapter ok line carrying a real duration rather than the no-tests-to-run suffix. The E2E suite was not executed; it takes a flock suite lock returning exit 73 when held, and this phase produced no source edit for it to cover.
